Not too long ago, Marcus Smart had one foot out the door in the NBA 😳

When he was traded to the Memphis Grizzlies, he was expected to be the guy to elevate them from a playoff team to a playoff contender.

Unfortunately, he was limited to 20 games due to injuries.

By the 2025 trade deadline, Smart was traded to a rebuilding team in the Washington Wizards for Johnny Davis and Marvin Bagley III... Two players who were gone by the offseason.

On the Wizards, Smart looked like he lost a step.

At 30 years old, he had career lows in minutes and eventually got waived.

But that's the duality of a role player like Smart.

On a rebuilding team, he's no better than the 10th or 12th man on the bench.

But on a playoff team?

He's the engine that gets everyone going.

Last offseason, Smart signed a two-year, $11 million deal with the Los Angeles Lakers.

His stats weren't 6MOY worthy.

But to the Lakers, he was one of the most important player on the team.

Like every good vet, Smart led by example.

He was a backup point guard, he dove for loose balls, and made all the winning plays.

Now he's on the Houston Rockets reunited with the coach who made him DPOY.

It's rare you see players thrive simply by doing the little things.

Marcus Smart built his career on it 💪
